# 1.29.0 — drag chats into folders, a working updater, faster large chats

Settings, keys and conversations from earlier versions are read as they are.

## Sidebar

- **Drag a chat into a folder, into Pinned, back into the main list or into the archive.** Hold
  the mouse button on a chat and move it: the section it will land in lights up, and a
  **Pin** zone appears at the top while nothing is pinned yet. Selected chats (Ctrl or Shift
  click) move together. Esc cancels. A chat dropped into a collapsed folder opens the folder so
  you can see it there.
- The chat list no longer scrolls when you drag it with the mouse button held — that gesture now
  moves chats. The wheel and the scroll bar work as before.
- The chat menu (**⋯** or right click) and the folder menu have icons.

## Settings

- Drop-down lists no longer show the page or the desktop through them with the *Glass* look: the
  list has a solid background and a shadow, and the selected item reads clearly in both themes.
  Tooltips got the same fix.

## Screenshots

A shortcut saved in **Settings → Windows → From any app** could take over a key combination that
Windows uses for screenshots (Win+Shift+S, Win+Shift+R, Win+G, Win+Alt+R, Win+Alt+G). Such a
shortcut is no longer registered, and the settings page refuses it with an explanation. The
program never blocks screen capture of its own window.

## Updating from inside the program works again

On many computers the program found a new version but would not install it: the **Update**
button was missing or vanished a little later, and auto-update downloaded nothing.

The program asks GitHub's API about new releases, and the API answers only 60 anonymous requests
per hour **per internet address**. Behind a VPN, a mobile network or a shared office connection,
other people's requests use up that limit. The program then fell back to GitHub's release page,
which tells the version number but not the download link — so there was nothing to install.

- **The fallback finds the file too.** When the API refuses or does not answer, the program reads
  the release's `SHA256SUMS` file straight from github.com, which the API limit does not cover.
  A version found this way gets an **Update** button and installs automatically, still verified
  by SHA-256 before it replaces anything.
- **More reasons to use the fallback**: any API error, an unreachable api.github.com, or an API
  that takes longer than 10 seconds.
- **A found build is never forgotten.** A later check that knows less about the same version no
  longer replaces what was already found.
- **The new version is named everywhere**: in the status line ("Downloading version 1.29.1 -
  37 %"), in the sidebar ("v1.29.0 · v1.29.1 available") and in failure messages.
- **The download can be cancelled**, and the card then goes back to the found version with its
  **Update** button.
- **A failed check says why** instead of "Up to date", with an **Open release** button.

If you are on 1.28.0 or older and see no **Update** button, download 1.29.0 from this page once
and replace the old file. After that the program updates itself again.

## Speed

- **Faster start.** The first launch of a version records which parts of the program it needed
  while starting; later launches prepare those parts in the background on spare processor cores
  while the window is being built. The record lives in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AmarinAdminAI\jit` and is
  replaced with each new version.
- **A lighter sidebar while a reply streams.** The chat list is checked several times a second
  during an answer. With many chats each check used to produce a sizeable amount of throwaway
  memory; it now reuses its buffers and its copy of the folders and tags until something actually
  changes.

## Large chats

- Zooming a large chat right after opening it no longer jitters or jumps: messages above the
  screen are built only while the transcript stands still, and the space reserved for them is
  estimated from their layout (code blocks, tables, headings), so far less moves when they are
  built.
- Background building of a long chat works in short time slices instead of fixed batches, so a
  message with a lot of code no longer stalls the window.
- The edit box under each of your messages is created only when you edit, which saves memory and
  time on long chats.
- A reply that was still being written when the program closed or crashed is shown as stopped,
  with **Continue**, instead of thinking forever.

## File

`Amarin-Admin-AI-v1.29.0-win-x64.exe` — a single file, nothing to unpack.
